_note.what_this_is: A curated lookup table mapping protein-complex and pathway names to UniProt accessions. It is NOT an inference engine and complex_resolve.py must never treat it as one. Membership of a complex is a claim about experiment, not something derivable from a name.
_note.curated: Every entry is added by hand. Nothing here is generated, predicted, or inferred from string similarity. If a complex is not in this file, the resolver returns empty with a reason -- absence is a correct answer and a guessed membership list is a fabrication that reads exactly like a retrieved one.
_note.source_required: Every entry and every component carries `source`: a citable reference for the membership claim, and where possible a structure that shows the subunits together. A component whose source cannot be produced is removed from the table, not left unsourced.
_note.sources_are_not_verified_by_the_tool: The resolver verifies ACCESSIONS against Paperclip at run time. It does not and cannot verify citations. The citation is the curator's warrant; a reader who doubts a membership claim must check the reference, not the tool output.
_note.absent_complex_returns_empty: No fuzzy fallback, no nearest-neighbour substitution, no 'probably means'. A name with no exact entry returns either a PROPOSAL (partial match, requires human confirmation, never an answer) or an empty result with a reason.
_note.pathway_is_not_a_complex: Entries with kind 'pathway' name a signalling route, not a physical assembly. They carry `candidates`, never `components`, and can never resolve to one complex or one accession. This distinction is the point of the file: 'TLR/IL-1R signaling' is in here precisely so that it fails loudly rather than quietly resolving to whichever receptor happens to be listed first.
_note.accessions_retrieved_not_recalled: All accessions below were returned by `paperclip sql -s proteins` against uniprot_v.proteins on 2026-08-15, filtered to organism = 'Homo sapiens'. None was written from memory.
not_retrieved: IL1RAP (IL-1 receptor accessory protein) -- the query timed out on three attempts and no accession was returned. It is therefore ABSENT from this table. A repeated timeout is a failed retrieval, not evidence the protein is missing from UniProt; do not read its absence here as a biological claim, and do not fill it in from memory.
_note.organism: All entries are human (Homo sapiens). Orthologues are not interchangeable and must be curated as separate entries.

schema.complex: carries `components` -- proteins with evidence of co-assembly
schema.pathway: carries `candidates` -- proteins on the route, with no principled way to pick one
schema.role: function within the assembly where a source states it; null where it does not
schema.membership: core (present in the cited structure/assembly) | receptor_proximal (associates at the receptor, outside the cited core) | proposed (reported as a component but not in the cited structure)

source.citation: Lin SC, Lo YC, Wu H. Helical assembly in the MyD88-IRAK4-IRAK2 complex in TLR/IL-1R signalling. Nature 2010;465:885-890.
source.note: Crystal structure of the death-domain assembly: 6 MyD88, 4 IRAK4, 4 IRAK2. This is the membership evidence for the three core subunits; it does not contain IRAK1.

components.protein_name: Myeloid differentiation primary response protein MyD88
components.source: Lin et al., Nature 2010 (PDB 3MOP) -- 6 copies in the assembled death-domain helix
components.note: The nucleating adaptor. Bridges the receptor TIR domain to the IRAK kinases; the interaction a PPI-disruption strategy would target sits here.

components.source: Lin et al., Nature 2010 (PDB 3MOP) -- 4 copies; catalytic activity per Motshwene et al., J Biol Chem 2009;284:25404-25411 (doi:10.1074/jbc.M109.022392)
components.note: Catalytically active Ser/Thr kinase AND a scaffold. Both functions are real and a small molecule that blocks the ATP site does not necessarily block the scaffolding role.

components.source: Motshwene PG et al., J Biol Chem 2009;284:25404-25411 (doi:10.1074/jbc.M109.022392); Gay NJ et al., Nat Rev Immunol 2014;14:546-558 (doi:10.1038/nri3713)
components.note: Catalytically active, recruited to and phosphorylated by IRAK4, but NOT present in the 3MOP structure -- IRAK2 occupies that position there. Membership is 'proposed' for that reason. IRAK1 and IRAK2 are reported as alternative occupants of the same layer rather than as simultaneous subunits; do not report a stoichiometry that includes both.

components.source: Lin et al., Nature 2010 (PDB 3MOP) -- 4 copies; pseudokinase assignment per Janssens S, Beyaert R. Mol Cell 2003;11:293-302
components.note: Catalytically inactive. It is in the complex as a scaffold, so an ATP-competitive small molecule has no mechanism against it -- relevant to which subunit a tractability review can actually address.

components.source: Gay NJ, Symmons MF, Gangloff M, Bryant CE. Assembly and localization of Toll-like receptor signalling complexes. Nat Rev Immunol 2014;14:546-558 (doi:10.1038/nri3713)
components.note: Also called Mal. Recruits MyD88 to TLR2 and TLR4 at the membrane. It is not a subunit of the 3MOP death-domain core, which is why membership is 'receptor_proximal' and not 'core'. Counting it as a Myddosome subunit overstates the structural evidence.

entries.name: TLR/IL-1R signaling
entries.not_a_complex_because: This names a signalling ROUTE, not a physical assembly. The route is entered through any of several receptors -- TLR4 and IL1R1 among them -- which do not co-assemble with each other and are not interchangeable. Nothing in the name selects one, and no rule can: TLR4 and IL1R1 are equally consistent with the phrase. Picking either would be a fabrication dressed as a resolution.
entries.what_to_do_instead: Return the full candidate list flagged as a pathway and hand the choice back. If an upstream evidence graph is the source, issue an expand_node / re-query for the specific receptor rather than choosing here. A resolved single accession is NOT an acceptable output for this entry under any circumstances.

source.citation: O'Neill LAJ, Bowie AG. The family of five: TIR-domain-containing adaptors in Toll-like receptor signalling. Nat Rev Immunol 2007;7:353-364.
source.note: Cited for the shape of the pathway -- multiple receptors converging on shared TIR adaptors -- which is the reason this entry cannot collapse to one protein.

candidates.note: One of several possible receptors. Listed first by accession sort order, which carries no meaning -- do not read list position as preference.
Included to make the point that the receptor set is open, not a choice between two.
The IL-1R arm. Equally consistent with the phrase as TLR4; this is the ambiguity, not a tie to break.

candidates.source: Gay NJ et al., Nat Rev Immunol 2014;14:546-558
candidates.note: Shared transducer, TLR2/TLR4 arm only -- not used by IL1R1, so its presence does not disambiguate the receptor either.

candidates.protein_name: Myeloid differentiation primary response protein MyD88
candidates.note: Common to both arms. Being downstream of every candidate receptor, it identifies the pathway but does not identify which receptor the evidence meant.

candidates.source: Motshwene PG et al., J Biol Chem 2009;284:25404-25411
candidates.note: Shared node downstream of both arms.

entries.name: TLR/MyD88/NF-kB signalling axis
entries.not_a_complex_because: Three-way axis names naming a receptor family, one adaptor, and a transcription factor that is itself a family of dimers. Two of the three ends are unresolvable: 'TLR' is a family of at least ten human receptors, and 'NF-kB' is a dimer drawn from a set of subunits (RELA and NFKB1 among them), not a single protein. Only the MyD88 waypoint resolves, and one resolved waypoint out of three does not make the phrase a complex.
entries.what_to_do_instead: Return the candidate list flagged as a pathway. The one unambiguous member (MYD88, Q99836) may be reported as such, but reporting it as THE resolution of the axis silently discards the TLR and NF-kB ends of the phrase.

source.citation: Gay NJ, Symmons MF, Gangloff M, Bryant CE. Assembly and localization of Toll-like receptor signalling complexes. Nat Rev Immunol 2014;14:546-558.
source.note: Cited for the receptor-to-adaptor-to-transcription-factor route. Membership of NF-kB dimers is a separate claim with a separate source and is not asserted here.
